Verumtamen, quantum ex textu perpenditur, videntur soli pastores angelos illos vidisse atque audisse: ut sit sensus, quod omnes qui audierunt a pastoribus, sint mirati. Unde expositorie subditur: et, pro id est, de his quæ dicta erant a pastoribus ad ipsos de puero isto, quod scilicet angelus de eo dixisset, et qualiter angelorum militia hymnum Domino cecinisset. De his, inquam, mirati sunt merito, quia supernaturale fuit, quod in una persona tanta majestas et tanta humilitas, tanta dominatio et tanta inopia convenissent, quod Rex cœlorum natus esset in terra, quod Desideratus cunctis gentibus advenisset, quem Patriarchæ atque Prophetæ tam ineffabiliter optaverunt. Insuper sunt mirati de tam constanti, certa ac fervida protestatione pastorum, qui inaudita fingere nescierunt, sed simplici facundia, quæ vera sunt prædicaverunt.
paras.en: [[2:18|And all that heard wondered|Et omnes qui audierant, mirati sunt]]. Some expound this thus: all who had heard from the angel these mysteries of Christ, namely how He had been born, wondered that Christ, the Lord of all, had been born in so mean a stable and laid in a manger, and yet proclaimed so solemnly by the angelic host. From which it would follow that the angels appeared not to the shepherds only, and that the angelic praise was not heard by the shepherds alone. But, so far as can be gathered from the text, the shepherds alone seem to have seen and heard those angels: so that the sense is that all who heard it from the shepherds wondered. Hence there is added by way of explanation: [[2:18|and at those things that were told them by the shepherds|et de his quæ dicta erant a pastoribus ad ipsos]] (*and* standing for *that is*) about this Child: namely what the angel had said of Him, and how the army of angels had sung a hymn to the Lord. At these things, I say, they rightly wondered, for it was beyond nature that in one person such majesty and such lowliness, such lordship and such want should come together; that the King of heaven should be born on earth; that the Desired of all nations[[Agg 2:8||]] should have come, whom the Patriarchs and Prophets had longed for so unspeakably. Moreover they wondered at the steadfast, sure and fervent testimony of the shepherds, who did not know how to invent things unheard of, but with simple eloquence proclaimed what was true.

paras.t: Maria autem: cujus est tanta suavitas, juxta Bernardum, ut nunquam piæ memoriæ portas ingrediatur absque insitæ sibi dulcedinis adspersione; conservabat omnia verba hæc, quæ jam de Christo conscripta sunt, hoc est, ea memoriæ diligentissime commendavit, conferens in corde suo, id est, intellectualiter ea revolvens, ubertimque repetens, atque ad invicem comparans. Itaque quietissima ac purissima Virgo delectabiliter consideravit, quomodo angelus sibi Christum annuntiasset, quomodo eum concepisset ac peperisset, quomodo angeli apparuerunt pastoribus, et quid pastores se vidisse atque audisse protestabantur, non solum Virgini gloriosæ et S. Joseph, sed et ceteris multis, quibus opportune poterant loqui. Hæc omnia sancta Virgo sapienter ac diligentissime consideravit, et ad Prophetarum de Christo prolata vaticinia comparavit: sicque vehementer profecit in fide, imo, secundum Ambrosium, a pastoribus fidem collegit, id est fidei incrementum, non quod unquam in fide ambigens fuerit, sed quia in cunctis quotidie profecit virtutibus. Hinc discipuli Christi, ab ipsa post Christi ascensionem de aliquibus dicuntur instructi. Præsertim inclytus iste evangelista Lucas ab ea edoctus asseritur, maxime in his quæ ipse solus de Christi infantia refert: non quod a Spiritu Sancto non sit de illis instructus, imo et Spiritus Sanctus eum per Mariam dignissimam sic instruxit, et supernaturali irradiatione de omnibus informavit, certificavit, infallibiliterque direxit. Eadem enim veritas a diversis et pluribus modis addiscitur, quia ab uno clarius et distinctius disci potest, quam ab alio, quantum ad se et ad circumstantias suas.
paras.en: [[2:19|But Mary|Maria autem]], whose sweetness is so great, according to Bernard, that she never enters the gates of a devout memory without sprinkling it with the sweetness that is hers, [[2:19|kept all these words|conservabat omnia verba hæc]] which have now been written about Christ; that is, she committed them most diligently to memory, [[2:19|pondering them in her heart|conferens in corde suo]], that is, turning them over in her understanding, going over them again and again, and comparing them with one another. So the most tranquil and most pure Virgin considered with delight how the angel had announced Christ to her, how she had conceived and brought Him forth, how the angels appeared to the shepherds, and what the shepherds declared they had seen and heard, not only to the glorious Virgin and St Joseph but to many others as well, to whom they had occasion to speak. All these things the holy Virgin considered wisely and most diligently, and compared them with the prophecies the Prophets had uttered about Christ: and so she made great progress in faith; nay, according to Ambrose, she gathered faith from the shepherds, that is, an increase of faith; not that she ever wavered in faith, but because she advanced daily in all the virtues. Hence the disciples of Christ are said to have been instructed by her about some things after Christ's ascension. In particular this renowned evangelist Luke is said to have been taught by her, especially in the things which he alone relates about the infancy of Christ: not that he was not instructed about them by the Holy Ghost; rather, the Holy Ghost instructed him in this way through the most worthy Mary, and by a supernatural enlightenment informed him of all, made him certain, and directed him infallibly. For the same truth is learned from different persons and in several ways, since it can be learned more clearly and distinctly from one than from another, as regards the thing itself and its circumstances.

paras.t: Præterea, juxta Ambrosium, discamus in omnibus sanctæ Virginis castitatem, quæ non minus ore pudica quam corpore, argumenta fidei conferebat in corde. Etenim virginalis pudicitiæ jura custodiens, secundum Bedam, secreta Christi quæ noverat, nemini tunc divulgavit, sed conferebat quæ legerat facienda, cum his quæ jam noverat facta. Verumtamen, puto quod familiaribus aliquibus et pie interrogantibus aliqua secrete aperuit, prout ratio postulavit et caritas. Itaque et nos beatissimæ Virginis exemplo, omnia divina atque salubria quæ audimus, videmus, scimus, seu legimus, memoriter teneamus, sagaciter conferamus, et juxta hæc, nostram conversationem in omnibus regulemus, ut cum Psalmista dicere mereamur: In corde meo abscondi eloquia tua, ut non peccem tibi. Nam et Christus testatur: Beati qui audiunt verbum Dei et custodiunt illud.
paras.en: Moreover, according to Ambrose, let us learn in all things the chastity of the holy Virgin, who, modest no less in speech than in body, pondered in her heart the proofs of faith. For, keeping the laws of virginal modesty, according to Bede, she disclosed to no one at that time the secrets of Christ which she knew, but compared what she had read was to be done with what she now knew had been done. Yet I think that she opened some things in secret to certain intimate friends who asked devoutly, as reason and charity required. Let us too, then, after the example of the most blessed Virgin, keep in memory all the divine and wholesome things we hear, see, know or read, compare them wisely, and order our life in all things according to them, so that we may deserve to say with the Psalmist: [[Ps 118:11|Thy words have I hidden in my heart, that I may not sin against thee.|In corde meo abscondi eloquia tua, ut non peccem tibi.]] For Christ also testifies: [[Luke 11:28|blessed are they who hear the word of God and keep it|Beati qui audiunt verbum Dei et custodiunt illud]].

paras.t: Et reversi sunt pastores ad pecora sua, quæ oves fuisse dicuntur, quamvis forte et aliqua alia pecora fuerunt: sicut et filii Jacob diversarum specierum pecora custodiebant, et tamen in Genesi pastores se ovium nominant; glorificantes, id est, gloriosum confitentes seu magnifice honorantes, et laudantes Deum, pro beneficiis suis, de quibus subjungitur: in omnibus magnalibus Dei, quæ audierant ab angelo exercituque angelico de Christi nativitate, etc., et viderant propriis oculis in Bethlehem, sicut dictum est ad illos. Hoc potest referri ad id quod ait, Glorificantes et laudantes Deum: ut sit sensus, quod Deum glorificabant atque laudabant sicut dictum est ad illos, id est, sicut audientibus eis angeli sancti fecerunt, dicendo: Gloria in altissimis Deo. Potest quoque referri ad id quod ait, Quæ audierant: eritque sensus, quod glorificabant Deum in omnibus quæ audierant et viderant sicut dictum est ad illos: id est, eo modo viderant sicut ab angelo fuit eis prædictum, et ideo Deum laudabant quia sic esse invenerunt.
paras.en: [[2:20|And the shepherds returned|Et reversi sunt pastores]] to their cattle, which are said to have been sheep, though perhaps there were some other cattle too: as the sons of Jacob also kept cattle of different kinds, and yet in Genesis they call themselves shepherds of sheep[[Gen 47:3||]] [the margin's numerals are partly unreadable (Gen. xl…, 3); the words *pastores ovium* stand at Gen 47:3 and 46:32]; [[2:20|glorifying|glorificantes]], that is, confessing Him glorious, or honouring Him magnificently, [[2:20|and praising God|et laudantes Deum]] for His benefits, of which it is added: *for all* the great works of God, [[2:20|the things they had heard|quæ audierant]] from the angel and the angelic host about the birth of Christ, etc., [[2:20|and seen|et viderant]] with their own eyes in Bethlehem, [[2:20|as it was told unto them|sicut dictum est ad illos]]. This can be referred to the words *glorifying and praising God*: so that the sense is that they glorified and praised God *as it was told unto them*, that is, as the holy angels had done in their hearing, saying: [[2:14|Glory to God in the highest|Gloria in altissimis Deo]]. It can also be referred to the words *the things they had heard*: and the sense will be that they glorified God for all they had heard and seen, *as it was told unto them*: that is, they had seen it in the way the angel had foretold to them, and so they praised God because they found it to be so.

paras.t: Postremo, quod pastores corporaliter peregerunt, nos spiritualiter faciamus. Hortemur nos mutuo, dicentes: Eamus usque Bethlehem, id est, per devotam et affectuosam considerationem uniamus cor nostrum loco in quo natus est Christus, et mentaliter intueamur quantam paupertatem et humilitatem pro nobis assumpsit Rex gloriæ, simusque grati beneficiis ejus verbo et opere, ipsum veraciter imitando, et cum angelicis spiritibus ardenter ac reverenter laudando.
paras.en: Lastly, what the shepherds did bodily, let us do spiritually. Let us exhort one another, saying: [[2:15|Let us go over to Bethlehem|Eamus usque Bethlehem]]; that is, by devout and loving consideration let us join our heart to the place where Christ was born, and gaze in mind at how great a poverty and lowliness the King of glory took on for us; and let us be grateful for His benefits in word and deed, imitating Him truly, and praising Him ardently and reverently with the angelic spirits.

paras.t: Subinde circumcisionem Christi Evangelista describit. Et postquam consummati sunt, id est impleti, dies octo a nativitate Christi, computando seu includendo tam nativitatis quam circumcisionis diem ipsius, ut circumcideretur puer, infantulus Jesus, de quo loquitur Isaias: Puer natus est nobis. Ly ut, tenetur hic concomitanter, quanquam etiam teneri posset aliquo modo causaliter, quoniam tanta est dignitas Salvatoris, ut ad ipsum et ad gesta ipsius, tempora ordinentur: quod de temporibus quibus vixit in sæculo isto specialiter dici potest. Vocatum est nomen ejus Jesus, quod interpretatur salvator, ad insinuandum quod ipse esset verus mundi Salvator, omnes in se credentes generaliter et complete atque finaliter a morte peccati, interituque inferni eripiens, et ad cœlestem felicitatem perducens. Unde in Matthæo, quum angelus dixisset ad Joseph, Vocabis nomen ejus Jesum, causam nominationis adjecit, dicendo: Ipse enim salvum faciet populum suum a peccatis eorum. De quo Isaias scribit: Dominus posuit in eo iniquitatem omnium nostrum: cujus livore sanati sumus. Et in Actibus Petrus inquit: Non est aliud nomen datum hominibus sub cœlo, in quo oporteat nos salvos fieri.
paras.en: Next the Evangelist describes the circumcision of Christ. [[2:21|And after eight days were accomplished|Et postquam consummati sunt dies octo]], that is, fulfilled, from the birth of Christ, counting or including both the day of His birth and that of His circumcision, [[2:21|that the child should be circumcised|ut circumcideretur puer]], the little Infant Jesus, of whom Isaias says: [[Is 9:6|a CHILD IS BORN to us|Puer natus est nobis]] [Denis has *Puer* where the Vulgate has *Parvulus*]. The word *ut* [“that”] is taken here as expressing what accompanies, though it could also in some way be taken as expressing cause, since the dignity of the Saviour is so great that the times are ordered to Him and to His deeds: which can be said especially of the times in which He lived in this world. [[2:21|his name was called Jesus|vocatum est nomen ejus Jesus]], which is interpreted *saviour*, to show that He was the true Saviour of the world, who rescues all who believe in Him, universally, completely and finally, from the death of sin and the destruction of hell, and leads them to heavenly happiness. Hence in Matthew, when the angel had said to Joseph, [[Matt 1:21|thou shalt call his name Jesus|Vocabis nomen ejus Jesum]], he added the reason for the name, saying: [[Matt 1:21|For he shall save his people from their sins|Ipse enim salvum faciet populum suum a peccatis eorum]]. Of whom Isaias writes: [[Is 53:6|the Lord hath laid on him the iniquity of us all|Dominus posuit in eo iniquitatem omnium nostrum]]: [[Is 53:5|by his bruises we are healed|cujus livore sanati sumus]]. And in the Acts Peter says: [[Acts 4:12|there is no other name under heaven given to men, whereby we must be saved|Non est aliud nomen datum hominibus sub cœlo, in quo oporteat nos salvos fieri]].

paras.t: Unde quod aliqui in veteri Testamento vocati sunt nomine isto, ut Josue, qui alio nomine dictus est Jesus, et Jesus filius Josedec, fuit alia ratione, et in figura Jesu Christi. Josue quippe salvavit filios Israel a Chananæis, et Jesus filius Josedec pontifex Judæorum, fuit unus reducentium eos de Babylone: quæ fuerunt particulares et imperfectæ liberationes, figurantes liberationem perfectam a Jesu Christo peractam. Itaque nomen istud, Jesus, fuit Christo novum et proprium, prout impositum est ad designandam liberationem completam. Ad quod multi allegant illud Isaiæ: Vocabitur tibi nomen novum, quod os Domini nominavit. Verumtamen, hoc ad litteram dicitur de Ecclesia seu Synagoga ad Christum conversa, non de Christo, quamvis possit aptari ad ipsum. Quod vocatum, id est expressum et prænuntiatum, seu vocari commissum, est ab angelo: nam apud Matthæum angelus legitur dixisse ad Joseph, Vocabis nomen ejus Jesum; et idem ait ad Virginem sanctam; priusquam in utero conciperetur, id est in ventre Mariæ virgineo de Spiritu Sancto. Ait enim angelus ad eam: Ne timeas, Maria, ecce concipies in utero et paries filium, et vocabis nomen ejus Jesum. Recteque dicitur, Quod vocatum est ab angelo, non, Impositum, quia jam ante a Deo fuit impositum, qui præordinavit Christum ita vocandum, et per angelum ac Mariam et Joseph ita vocavit eumdem, quemadmodum Christus per Isaiam testatur: Dominus ab utero vocavit me, de ventre matris meæ recordatus est nominis mei.
paras.en: So the fact that some in the Old Testament were called by this name, such as Josue, who by another name was called Jesus[[Ecclus 46:1||]], and Jesus the son of Josedec[[Ecclus 49:14||]], was for another reason, and in figure of Jesus Christ. For Josue saved the children of Israel from the Chanaanites[[Jos 11:23||]], and Jesus the son of Josedec, high priest of the Jews, was one of those who brought them back from Babylon[[1 Esd 3:2||]]: and these were partial and imperfect deliverances, figuring the perfect deliverance accomplished by Jesus Christ. So this name, *Jesus*, was new and proper to Christ, inasmuch as it was given to signify complete deliverance. For this many allege the words of Isaias: [[Is 62:2|thou shalt be called by a new name, which the mouth of the Lord shall name|Vocabitur tibi nomen novum, quod os Domini nominavit]]. But this is said literally of the Church, or of the Synagogue converted to Christ, not of Christ, though it can be applied to Him. [[2:21|which was called by the angel|Quod vocatum est ab angelo]], that is, expressed and foretold, or committed to be called: for in Matthew the angel is read to have said to Joseph, [[Matt 1:21|thou shalt call his name Jesus|Vocabis nomen ejus Jesum]]; and the same angel said it to the holy Virgin, [[2:21|before he was conceived in the womb|priusquam in utero conciperetur]], that is, in the virginal womb of Mary, by the Holy Ghost. For the angel said to her: [[Luke 1:30|Fear not, Mary|Ne timeas, Maria]], [[Luke 1:31|Behold thou shalt conceive in thy womb and shalt bring forth a son: and thou shalt call his name Jesus|ecce concipies in utero et paries filium, et vocabis nomen ejus Jesum]]. And rightly it says *which was called by the angel*, not *given*, because it had already been given beforehand by God, who foreordained that Christ should be so called, and through the angel, and Mary and Joseph, so called Him: as Christ testifies through Isaias: [[Is 49:1|The Lord hath called me from the womb, from the bowels of my mother he hath been mindful of my name|Dominus ab utero vocavit me, de ventre matris meæ recordatus est nominis mei]].

paras.t: Præterea, ut aliqui dicunt, Jesus dicitur Salvator: Primo, a potentia salvandi: sicque convenit sibi nomen hoc ab æterno, videlicet secundum suam divinitatem, qua ab æterno habuit potestatem salvandi. Secundo, ab habitu salvandi: et sic impositum fuit sibi ab angelo, et competit ei a primo suæ conceptionis instanti, in quo secundum humanitatem suam accepit gratiam tam perfectam, qua postea fecit et pertulit ea per quæ actualiter mundum salvavit. Tertio, ab actu salvandi: sicque vocatum fuit nomen istud in circumcisione, et competit Christo ratione suæ passionis; in circumcisione autem primo sanguinem suum fudit pro nobis. Insuper intuendum, quod salvare competit Christo secundum utramque suam naturam: quia secundum divinitatem competit ei auctoritative et principaliter, secundum humanitatem vero instrumentaliter, ut supra dictum est plenius: ideo secundum utramque naturam Jesus potest vocari. Siquidem de Deo uno ac trino scriptum est in Habacuc: Ego autem in Domino gaudebo, et exsultabo in Deo Jesu meo. Sed nunc tractatur de nomine isto prout competit Christo secundum naturam humanam.
paras.en: Moreover, as some say, Jesus is called Saviour: first, from the power of saving: and in this way the name belongs to Him from eternity, namely according to His divinity, by which from eternity He had the power to save. Secondly, from the habit of saving [that is, the abiding capacity for it]: and in this way it was given Him by the angel, and belongs to Him from the first instant of His conception, in which according to His humanity He received grace so perfect that by it He afterwards did and suffered the things by which He actually saved the world. Thirdly, from the act of saving: and in this way the name was called at the circumcision, and belongs to Christ by reason of His passion; for in the circumcision He first shed His blood for us. We must also observe that saving belongs to Christ according to each of His natures: according to His divinity as author and principal cause, but according to His humanity as instrument, as was said more fully above: and so He can be called Jesus according to each nature. For of God, one and three, it is written in Habacuc: [[Hab 3:18|But I will rejoice in the Lord: and I will joy in God my Jesus.|Ego autem in Domino gaudebo; et exsultabo in Deo Jesu meo.]] But here the name is treated as it belongs to Christ according to His human nature.

paras.t: Denique, secundum Epiphanium, pluribus de causis Christus voluit circumcidi: Primo, ut ostenderet se veraciter incarnatum, non phantastice seu apparenter, ut Manichæus confinxit. Secundo, ut monstraret quod corpus suum divinitati consubstantiale non esset, ut Apollinaris rudissime dixit; item ad declarandum quod non detulit illud de cœlo, ut Valentinus asseruit. Rursus et tertio, ne Judæi haberent occasionem contra Christum, dicendo quod legem transgressus esset, circumcisionem non accipiendo. Quarto, ut legem impleret et approbaret, atque exemplum humilitatis ac obedientiæ daret: propter quod postea fatebatur, Non veni legem solvere, sed implere. Jussum autem fuit divinitus in Genesi: Infans octo dierum circumcidetur in vobis. Quinto, ut virtute ac merito suæ circumcisionis, fideles suos a duritia præcepti illius exoneraret, et ipsam circumcisionem in Baptismum dulciter commutaret. Sexto, ut Judæorum scandalum evitaret. Septimo, propter communitatis et uniformitatis commendationem, ut et nos singularitatem vitemus, nec pro peccatis nostris puniri spernamus, videntes quod Christus, qui remedio culpæ non eguit, circumcisionem, quæ fuit remedium contra originale peccatum, ineffabili humanitate suscepit. Unde ad Hebræos Apostolus: Debuit, inquit, per omnia fratribus assimilari. Postremo, circumcisionem accipiendo, abstulit diabolo occasionem suspicandi quod ipse esset Christus.
paras.en: Again, according to Epiphanius, Christ willed to be circumcised for several reasons. First, to show that He was truly incarnate, not in appearance or seeming, as Manichæus feigned. Secondly, to show that His body was not consubstantial with the divinity, as Apollinaris most crudely said; and also to declare that He did not bring it down from heaven, as Valentinus asserted. Thirdly, that the Jews might have no occasion against Christ, saying that He had transgressed the law by not receiving circumcision. Fourthly, to fulfil and approve the law, and to give an example of humility and obedience: for which reason He afterwards declared: [[Matt 5:17|I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil|Non veni legem solvere, sed implere]]. Now it was commanded by God in Genesis: [[Gen 17:12|An infant of eight days old shall be circumcised among you|Infans octo dierum circumcidetur in vobis]]. Fifthly, that by the power and merit of His circumcision He might free His faithful from the harshness of that precept, and sweetly change circumcision itself into Baptism. Sixthly, to avoid scandal to the Jews. Seventhly, to commend what is common and uniform, so that we too may avoid singularity and not disdain to be punished for our sins, seeing that Christ, who had no need of a remedy for sin, took on Himself with unspeakable kindness circumcision, which was the remedy against original sin. Hence the Apostle says to the Hebrews: [[Heb 2:17|it behoved him in all things to be made like unto his brethren|Debuit, inquit, per omnia fratribus assimilari]]. Lastly, by receiving circumcision He took from the devil the occasion of suspecting that He was the Christ.

paras.t: Itaque et nos, universa quæ pro nostra salute Christus assumpsit, fecit ac pertulit, diligentissime consideremus, eique grati esse nitamur, ac spiritualiter circumcidamur, omnem inordinationem ac superfluitatem intus ac foris, videlicet in vestibus, verbis, operibus, otiis, omissionibus, itemque in cogitationibus, affectionibus, intentionibus, vitare conantes, nec aspera pœnitentiæ exercitia abominantes, sed viriliter amplectentes, quum et Christus in tam infantili ætate tam acerbum pro nobis dolorem subierit. Ut enim Rabbi Moyses testatur, in circumcisione fuit gravissimus dolor, in tantum quod multi infantes inde obierint. Hinc secundum eumdem, voluit Dominus pueros circumcidi die octava, quando adhuc modicam habent imaginationem, ut per hoc minus affligerentur. Quum ergo puer Jesus fuerit optimæ atque tenerrimæ complexionis ac perfectissimæ imaginationis a principio incarnationis, quemadmodum et plenissimæ intellectualis cognitionis, facile possumus advertere, quam gravissimam senserit pœnam in circumcisione, quam intime etiam ac pœnose ei compatiebatur affectuosissima atque piissima Genitrix ejus. Unde et nos compati utrique debemus.
paras.en: Let us too, then, consider most diligently all that Christ took on, did and suffered for our salvation, and strive to be grateful to Him, and be circumcised spiritually, trying to avoid all disorder and excess within and without, in clothing, words, works, idleness and omissions, and also in thoughts, affections and intentions; not shrinking from the harsh exercises of penance but embracing them manfully, since Christ too, at so infant an age, underwent so bitter a pain for us. For, as Rabbi Moses [Maimonides] testifies, there was very great pain in circumcision, so much that many infants died of it. Hence, according to the same author, the Lord willed boys to be circumcised on the eighth day, when they still have little power of imagination, so that they might suffer less from it. Since, then, the Child Jesus was from the beginning of the incarnation of the best and tenderest constitution and of the most perfect imagination, as also of the fullest intellectual knowledge, we can easily perceive how very grievous a pain He felt in the circumcision, and how inwardly and painfully His most loving and most tender Mother suffered with Him. And so we too ought to suffer with them both.

paras.t: At vero circa illud, Vocatum est nomen ejus Jesus, loquitur Origenes: Nomen Jesus gloriosum, omnique cultu dignissimum, nomen quod est super omne nomen, non decuit primum ab hominibus appellari, neque ab eis afferri in mundum, sed ab excellentiori natura. De cujus etiam nominis suavitate ait Bernardus: Nomen hoc Jesus, est mel in ore, in aure melos, in corde jubilus.
paras.en: On the words [[2:21|his name was called Jesus|Vocatum est nomen ejus Jesus]], Origen says: The glorious name of Jesus, most worthy of all worship, the [[Phil 2:9|name which is above all names|nomen quod est super omne nomen]], was not fit to be first spoken by men, nor brought into the world by them, but by a more excellent nature. And of the sweetness of this name Bernard says: This name Jesus is honey in the mouth, music in the ear, a song of joy in the heart.

2.title: Prosecutio expositionis hujus capituli secundi, ab eo loco: Et postquam impleti sunt dies purgationis ejus secundum legem Moysis
2.title_en: Continuation of the exposition of this second chapter, from the place: “And after the days of her purification, according to the law of Moses, were accomplished”

paras.t: Descripta Christi circumcisione, prosequitur Evangelista de ejus virgineæ Matris purificatione, omissa descriptione apparitionis Christi qua Magis innotuit, quam a Matthæo evangelista agnovit satis descriptam. Et postquam impleti sunt dies purgationis ejus, puta Mariæ, secundum legem Moysis, id est, quadraginta impletis diebus a Christi nativitate: in quorum ultimo infantulus fuit, secundum legem Moysis, in templo præsentandus, seu Domino offerendus; infra quos etiam dies mater, secundum legem Mosaicam, ab ingressu templi abstinuit, et quadragesimo die templum ingrediens, purificabatur. Præcepit etenim lex in Levitico, ut mulier, quæ suscepto semine masculum peperisset, immunda esset septem diebus, immunda equidem a consortio hominum ingressuque templi; et die octavo circumcideretur infantulus, ipsa quoque tunc munda efficeretur quoad consortium hominum; insuper post septem dies præfatos, maneret mulier adhuc triginta tribus diebus in sanguine purgationis suæ, abstinens ab introitu templi, non a consortio hominum; sic quadragesimo die offerret vel præsentaret puerum in templo, offerens simul munera secundum legem pro se et pro illo. Porro, si feminam peperisset, duplicabantur dies, tam quoad templi ingressum, quam ad consortium hominum.
paras.en: Having described the circumcision of Christ, the Evangelist goes on to the purification of His virgin Mother, leaving out the description of Christ's manifestation by which He was made known to the Magi[[Matt 2:1||]], which he knew had been sufficiently described by Matthew the evangelist. [[2:22|And after the days of her purification|Et postquam impleti sunt dies purgationis ejus]], that is, of Mary, [[2:22|according to the law of Moses, were accomplished|secundum legem Moysis]]: that is, when forty days from the birth of Christ were fulfilled; on the last of which the infant was to be presented in the temple, or offered to the Lord, according to the law of Moses; and within those days the mother too, according to the Mosaic law, kept away from entering the temple, and on the fortieth day, entering the temple, she was purified. For the law commanded in Leviticus that a woman who, [[Lev 12:2|having received seed shall bear a man child, she shall be unclean seven days|suscepto semine masculum peperisset, immunda esset septem diebus]]: unclean, that is, as regards the company of men and entering the temple; and on the eighth day the infant was to be circumcised, and she too then became clean as regards the company of men; further, after the said seven days the woman was to remain yet three and thirty days in the blood of her purification, keeping away from entering the temple, but not from the company of men[[Lev 12:4||]]; and so on the fortieth day she was to offer or present the child in the temple, offering at the same time gifts according to the law for herself and for him. And if she had borne a girl, the days were doubled, both as to entering the temple and as to the company of men.

paras.t: Sed quoniam Virgo beatissima, non semine suscepto concepit, verum virtute Spiritus Sancti, constat quod legi illi non fuit adstricta, nec eguit purgatione, quæ nec in peccato concepit, nec unquam peccavit, nec aliis matribus communem sustinuit fluxum, imo mente et corpore immaculatissima atque purissima peperit. Itaque dies isti dicuntur dies purgationis Mariæ, non secundum realem exsistentiam, sed secundum hominum æstimationem, quemadmodum Joseph pater Christi vocatur, quia sic putabatur; et quia secundum Hieronymum, consuetudo Scripturæ est gesta ita referre, quomodo tunc quando fiebant, fieri putabantur. Insuper, hoc modo dicuntur dies purgationis Mariæ secundum legem Moysis, quamvis secundum veritatem, lex illa super Mariam non caderet. Vel, dies purgationis ejus dicuntur impleti secundum legem Moysis, non quoad obligationem Mariæ ad purgationem, sed quantum ad determinationem impletionemque temporis. Voluit autem Maria dignissime subjici legi et quasi purgari in templo, ad dandum obedientiæ ac humilitatis exemplum, ad vitandum scandalum Judæorum, ad conformandum se aliis mulieribus in licitis ac honestis, et quoniam Filium suum vidit legi circumcisionis subjectum. Perfecta quippe obedientia plus peragit quam tenetur, dicente Bernardo: Perfecta obedientia legem nescit, terminis non arctatur; nec contenta angustiis professionis, largiori voluntate fertur secundum latitudinem caritatis.
paras.en: But since the most blessed Virgin conceived not by receiving seed but by the power of the Holy Ghost, it is certain that she was not bound by that law, nor needed purification: she who neither conceived in sin, nor ever sinned, nor underwent the flow common to other mothers, but brought forth most immaculate and most pure in mind and body. So these days are called the days of Mary's purification, not according to what really was, but according to men's reckoning: as Joseph is called the father of Christ, because he was so thought to be[[3:23||]]; and because, according to Jerome, it is the custom of Scripture to relate things done in the way in which they were thought to be done at the time they were done. Further, the days of Mary's purification are said in this way to be *according to the law of Moses*, although in truth that law did not fall upon Mary. Or, the days of her purification are said to be accomplished *according to the law of Moses* not as regards any obligation of Mary to be purified, but as regards the fixing and fulfilling of the time. And Mary most worthily willed to be subject to the law and, as it were, to be purified in the temple: to give an example of obedience and humility, to avoid scandal to the Jews, to conform herself to other women in what is lawful and becoming, and because she saw her Son subject to the law of circumcision. For perfect obedience does more than it is bound to, as Bernard says: Perfect obedience knows no law, is not confined by limits; nor, content with the narrow bounds of its profession, is it carried by a more generous will according to the breadth of charity.

paras.t: Tulerunt illum, scilicet Jesum, Maria et Joseph. Tunc enim egressa est Virgo Christifera stabulum in quo peperit Christum, tulitque eum ad templum (et forte sæpenumero ipsa cum Joseph detulit puerum in Jerusalem), ut sisterent, hoc est, offerrent, præsentarent, seu consecrarent, eum Domino, hoc est Deo Patri seu Deo trino ac simplici, quia et sibi ipsi secundum quod Deus est: quia offerri competit ei secundum humanitatem; sicut scriptum est in lege Domini, videlicet in Numeris et Exodo: Quia omne masculinum adaperiens vulvam, id est, primo eam nascendo aperiens, hoc est omne primogenitum tam in hominibus quam in pecoribus, sanctum Domino vocabitur, id est, consecrabitur Deo, ita quod ei offeretur, mancipatumque erit quasi ad ipsum specialiter pertinens. Unde per Moysen Dominus ait frequenter: Ex quo percussi omne primogenitum Ægypti, tam in hominibus quam in jumentis, sanctificavi mihi omne quod primo aperit vulvam in Israel, tam in hominibus quam in jumentis. Unde sanctificatio illa fuit deputatio quædam rerum illarum ad Deum, cujus magnificentia in rebus illis repræsentabatur, in quantum commemorabant occisionem primogenitorum Ægypti.
paras.en: [[2:22|they carried him|Tulerunt illum]], namely Jesus, Mary and Joseph. For then the Virgin who bore Christ went out of the stable in which she had brought forth Christ, and carried Him to the temple (and perhaps she often brought the child to Jerusalem with Joseph), [[2:22|to present him to the Lord|ut sisterent eum Domino]]: that is, to offer, present or consecrate Him to the Lord, that is, to God the Father, or to God three and simple, and so to Himself also as He is God; for to be offered belongs to Him according to His humanity; [[2:23|As it is written in the law of the Lord|sicut scriptum est in lege Domini]], namely in Numbers[[Num 8:16||]] and Exodus[[Ex 13:2||]] [the margin reads Num. vii (perhaps viii) and Exod. xiii, 2, 12–15]: [[2:23|Every male opening the womb|Quia omne masculinum adaperiens vulvam]], that is, opening it first by being born, that is, every firstborn, of men as of beasts, [[2:23|shall be called holy to the Lord|sanctum Domino vocabitur]], that is, shall be consecrated to God, so that it shall be offered to Him and made over to Him, as belonging to Him in a special way. Hence the Lord says often by Moses: [[Num 3:13|since I struck the firstborn in the land of Egypt: I have sanctified to myself|ex quo percussi primogenitos in terra Ægypti, sanctificavi mihi]] all that first openeth the womb in Israel, as well of men as of beasts[[Num 8:17||]][[Ex 13:12||]]. So that sanctification was a certain assigning of those things to God, whose magnificence was represented in them, inasmuch as they called to mind the slaying of the firstborn of Egypt.

paras.t: Primogenita autem diversimode Domino consecrabantur. Si enim fuerunt de tribu Levi et maculam non habebant, Deo jugiter ministrabant in templo, quando fuerunt adultæ ætatis, quamvis post oblationem mitterentur in domo parentum. Si vero fuerunt de aliqua aliarum undecim tribuum Israel, ex oblatione fuerant Dei, sed quinque siclis redimebantur. Si autem erant primogenita pecorum, et animalia munda, Domino offerebantur, nec redimebantur, sed sacerdotum erant, videlicet ad usum eorum. Quod si immunda fuerunt, redimebantur seu in aliud commutabantur, ut primogenitum asini in primogenitum ovis; vel occidebantur, ut primogenitum canis. Quoniam ergo Christus fuit de tribu Juda, constat quod quinque siclis redimebatur.
paras.en: Now the firstborn were consecrated to the Lord in different ways. If they were of the tribe of Levi and had no blemish, they ministered to God continually in the temple when they were of full age, although after the offering they were sent back to their parents' house. But if they were of any of the other eleven tribes of Israel, by the offering they were God's, but they were redeemed for five sicles[[Num 18:15||]][[Num 18:16||]]. And if they were the firstborn of cattle, and clean animals, they were offered to the Lord and not redeemed, but belonged to the priests, that is, for their use. But if they were unclean, they were redeemed or exchanged for something else, as the firstborn of an ass for the firstborn of a sheep[[Ex 13:13||]]; or they were killed, as the firstborn of a dog. Since, then, Christ was of the tribe of Juda, it is certain that He was redeemed for five sicles.

paras.t: Et ut darent, hoc est, etiam ideo tulerunt Jesum ad templum, ut offerrent pro ipso et matre ejus, hostiam secundum quod dictum est in lege Domini in Levitico, utpote par turturum aut duos pullos columbarum. Offerebaturque unus turtur Deo in holocaustum, alius pro peccato, qui cessit in usum sacerdotis orantis pro muliere quæ sic purgabatur. Hæc quoque fuit oblatio pauperum, nam divites agnum offerebant: ex quo patet paupertas Mariæ et Joseph. Verumtamen Maria a parentibus suis hereditatem bonam suscepit, nec dubium quin tres Magi in die Epiphaniæ pretiosa Christo dona obtulerint; sed perfectissima Virgo, inspirante ei spiritu Filii sui, omnia tenuissimæ necessitati, hoc est parcissimo victui atque tegumento, superflua, per se, vel potius per manus Joseph, erogavit egenis. Nec reor quod peregrinationi suæ cum Jesu et Joseph in Ægyptum aliquid notabile servaverit, vel tantam de crastino habuerit curam: quippe cujus spes in Deo perfectissima fuit, et quæ noverat se Christum Dei sapientiam ac providentiam omnipotentem secum habere in filium.
paras.en: [[2:24|And to offer|Et ut darent]]: that is, they carried Jesus to the temple for this reason also, to offer for Him and His mother [[2:24|a sacrifice, according as it is written in the law of the Lord|hostiam secundum quod dictum est in lege Domini]], in Leviticus, namely [[2:24|a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons|par turturum aut duos pullos columbarum]][[Lev 12:8||]]. And one turtle was offered to God as a holocaust, the other for sin, which went to the use of the priest who prayed for the woman thus purified. This too was the offering of the poor, for the rich offered a lamb[[Lev 12:6||]]: from which the poverty of Mary and Joseph is plain. Yet Mary had received a good inheritance from her parents, and there is no doubt that the three Magi on the day of the Epiphany offered precious gifts to Christ; but the most perfect Virgin, by the inspiration of the spirit of her Son, gave away to the needy, herself or rather by the hands of Joseph, all that went beyond the barest necessity, that is, the most sparing food and clothing. Nor do I think that she kept back anything notable for her journey with Jesus and Joseph into Egypt, or took so much care for the morrow: she whose hope in God was most perfect, and who knew that she had with her as her son Christ, the wisdom of God[[1 Cor 1:24||]] and His almighty providence.

paras.t: Circa hæc exclamat Cyrillus: O profunditatem sapientiæ et scientiæ Dei! Offert hostias, qui per singulas hostias honoratur cum Patre; figuras legis custodit veritas; qui legis est conditor ut Deus, legem custodit ut homo.
paras.en: On these things Cyril exclaims: [[Rom 11:33|O the depth of the riches of the wisdom and of the knowledge of God!|O profunditatem sapientiæ et scientiæ Dei!]]! He offers victims who in every victim is honoured with the Father; the Truth keeps the figures of the law; He who as God is the maker of the law keeps the law as man.

paras.t: Insuper ait: Videndum quid ista designent. Nimirum inter aves loquacissima est turtur, columba vero est animal mansuetum: sicque per utrumque Christus exprimitur, qui perfectæ mansuetudinis fuit, et suis sermonibus mundum convertit. Unde ad ejus passionem præfigurandam, columba et turtur oblatæ occidebantur. — Iterum, per columbam simplicitas, sive (ut dictum est) mititas, per turturem castitas designatur. Turtur namque si semel perdiderit conjugem, aliam non requirit. Ideo, secundum Athanasium, jussit Deus bina offerri, quoniam ex corpore et anima homine exsistente, duplicem poscit a nobis Deus castitatem ac mansuetudinem, videlicet animæ et corporis: alioqui erit homo hypocrita, gerens tegumentum occultæ malitiæ. Amplius autem, non absque mysterio Evangelista turtures et columbas diversimode exprimit, dicens, Par turturum aut duos pullos columbarum, non, Par columbarum. Turtur namque in omni sua ætate castum est animal, columba vero in perfecta ætate valde est luxuriosa, ideo decuit eam offerri in illa ætate in qua luxui non est apta, puta in juventute: ideo dicitur, Pullos columbarum, ad innuendum quod lascivia Deo displiceat. Postremo, Lucas non exprimit determinate quid Maria et Joseph obtulerint, an scilicet par turturum, aut duos pullos columbarum, quia redit in idem quidquid horum obtulisse dicantur. Per utrumque enim eorum inopia designatur, et res per utrumque illorum figurata, Deo est placita.
paras.en: Further he says: We must see what these signify. Among birds the turtle is the most talkative, while the dove is a gentle creature: and so by both Christ is expressed, who was of perfect gentleness, and converted the world by His words. Hence, to prefigure His passion, the dove and the turtle, when offered, were slain. — Again, by the dove simplicity, or (as was said) mildness, is signified; by the turtle, chastity. For the turtle, if once it has lost its mate, does not seek another. Therefore, according to Athanasius, God commanded two to be offered, because, since man consists of body and soul, God asks of us a twofold chastity and gentleness, namely of soul and of body: otherwise a man will be a hypocrite, wearing a covering of hidden malice. Moreover, not without a mystery does the Evangelist speak differently of the turtles and the doves, saying *a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons*, not “a pair of pigeons”. For the turtle is a chaste creature at every age, but the dove at full age is very lustful; so it was fitting that it be offered at the age at which it is not apt for lust, namely in youth: and so it says *young pigeons*, to hint that wantonness displeases God. Lastly, Luke does not say definitely what Mary and Joseph offered, whether a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons, because it comes to the same whichever of these they are said to have offered. For by either of them poverty is signified, and the thing figured by either of them is pleasing to God.

paras.t: Subinde describitur qualiter a testibus fide dignissimis Christus in præsentatione præfata testimonium habuit. Et ecce. Per demonstrativum hoc, Ecce, insinuatur magnum, notabile, attentioneque dignum esse quod subditur. Homo. Non enim hic homo dicitur ab eo quod in hominibus communiter prævalet, quod est sensualitas (juxta quem modum ait Apostolus Corinthiis scribens: Quum sit inter vos zelus et contentio, nonne homines estis?), sed prout homo dicitur ab eo quod in homine exstat præstantius, et quod in sapientibus prævalet, quod est ratio et pietas, juxta id quod dicit Apostolus: Si secundum hominem ad bestias pugnavi Ephesi. Cujus verbi iste est sensus: Si, pro Quia, secundum hominem, id est rationabiliter, ad bestias, hoc est contra homines bestiales ac perfidos, pugnavi, id est disputavi, Ephesi, hoc est in civitate quæ Ephesus nominatur. Unde humanum vocamus, quod rationabile est et pium. Hinc quidam hominem quasi describendo, hominem affirmant: Homo est animal mansuetum natura, erectum statura, discretumque ratione. Erat in Jerusalem: quæ sancta civitas dicitur, quoniam ibi erat templum, et viguit cultus divinus, studiumque legis ac Prophetarum; præsertim, quoniam Christus ibidem in templo oblatus est, prædicavit, miracula fecit, passus est, et sanguinem fudit, et deinde Spiritum Sanctum misit. Ibi demum primitiva Ecclesia sanctissime vixit. Cui nomen Simeon: et inter sacerdotes fuit famosus atque grandævus.
paras.en: Next it is described how Christ, at the said presentation, received testimony from witnesses most worthy of belief. [[2:25|And behold|Et ecce]]. By this demonstrative word *behold* it is hinted that what follows is great, notable and worthy of attention. [[2:25|a man|Homo]]. For he is not here called a man from what commonly prevails in men, which is sensuality (in the way in which the Apostle says, writing to the Corinthians: [[1 Cor 3:3|whereas there is among you envying and contention|Quum sit inter vos zelus et contentio]], are you not men? [Denis reads *homines*, “men”, where the Vulgate has *carnales*, “carnal”]), but as man is named from what is more excellent in man and prevails in the wise, which is reason and piety; according to what the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 15:32|If (according to man) I fought with beasts at Ephesus|Si secundum hominem ad bestias pugnavi Ephesi]]. The sense of which saying is: *If*, for “since”, *according to man*, that is, reasonably, *I fought*, that is, disputed, *with beasts*, that is, against bestial and faithless men, *at Ephesus*, that is, in the city called Ephesus. Hence we call *human* what is reasonable and kind. Hence some, as it were describing man, declare: Man is an animal gentle by nature, erect in stature, and distinguished by reason. [[2:25|in Jerusalem|Erat in Jerusalem]]: which is called the holy city, because the temple was there, and the worship of God flourished there, and the study of the law and the Prophets; above all because Christ was offered there in the temple, preached, worked miracles, suffered and shed His blood, and afterwards sent the Holy Ghost. There, lastly, the primitive Church lived most holily. [[2:25|named Simeon|Cui nomen Simeon]]: and he was renowned among the priests, and of great age.

paras.t: Et homo iste justus, justitia quæ est virtus cardinalis ac specialis, qua unicuique datur quod suum est, itemque justitia quæ est virtus generalis et virtualiter omnis virtus, quia omni virtute fuit ornatus. Fuitque præcipue caritativus ac justus, quia non proprium privatumque commodum, sed bonum commune, et generalem omnium desideravit salutem. Et timoratus, timore casto, sancto ac filiali, qui timet Dei offensam, et clementissimum Deum ut patrem inhonorare abhorret. De quo in Ecclesiastico scriptum est: Nihil melius quam timere Deum; et, Timor Dei super omnia se posuit. De quo ait Psalmista: Timete Dominum, omnes sancti ejus, quoniam nihil deest timentibus Deum. Quamvis ergo hic Simeon cunctis polleret virtutibus, tamen in justitia et timore fulsit præclarius, secundum quod quilibet Sanctorum dicitur in aliqua virtute amplius splenduisse. Propter quod de unoquoque cantatur: Non est inventus similis illi qui conservaret legem Excelsi. Unde et Paulus: Unusquisque, inquit, suum donum habet a Deo. Ideo de his duabus virtutibus specialiter commendatur. Itaque justus fuit ad proximum, timoratus ad Deum. Denique timor retrahit a peccato hominem, quemadmodum scriptum est: Per timorem declinat unusquisque a malo: ideo per timorem implevit quod dicitur, Declina a malo. Justitia autem bonum prosequitur: per quam implevit quod additur, Et fac bonum.
paras.en: [[2:25|and this man was just|et homo iste justus]], with the justice that is a cardinal and special virtue, by which to each is given what is his; and also with the justice that is a general virtue and virtually every virtue, since he was adorned with every virtue. And he was above all charitable and just, because he desired not his own private advantage, but the common good and the general salvation of all. [[2:25|and devout|Et timoratus]] [*timoratus*, literally “fearing”: Denis expounds it of the fear of God; the Douay-Rheims has “devout”], with a chaste, holy and filial fear, which fears to offend God and shrinks from dishonouring the most clement God as a father. Of which it is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 23:37|there is nothing better than the fear of God|Nihil melius quam timere Deum]]; and: [[Ecclus 25:14|The fear of God hath set itself above all things|Timor Dei super omnia se posuit]]. Of which the Psalmist says: [[Ps 33:10|Fear the Lord, all ye his saints: for there is no want to them that fear him|Timete Dominum, omnes sancti ejus, quoniam nihil deest timentibus Deum]] [Denis's wording, *nihil deest timentibus Deum*, differs slightly from the Vulgate's *non est inopia timentibus eum*]. Although, then, this Simeon was strong in all the virtues, yet he shone more brightly in justice and fear, in the way that each of the Saints is said to have been more resplendent in some one virtue. Wherefore of each one it is sung: [[Ecclus 44:20|there was not found the like to him|Non est inventus similis illi]] who kept the law of the most High [the words, said of Abraham in Ecclesiasticus, are sung in the Church's office of confessors]. Hence Paul too says: [[1 Cor 7:7|every one hath his proper gift from God|Unusquisque, inquit, suum donum habet a Deo]]. Therefore he is commended especially for these two virtues. So he was just towards his neighbour, devout towards God. Further, fear draws a man back from sin, as it is written: [[Prov 15:27|by the fear of the Lord every one declineth from evil|Per timorem declinat unusquisque a malo]]; so by fear he fulfilled what is said: [[Ps 36:27|Decline from evil|Declina a malo]]. But justice pursues the good: by it he fulfilled what is added: [[Ps 36:27|and do good|Et fac bonum]].

paras.t: Exspectans, hoc est, certissime affectuoseque sperans ac præstolans, consolationem Israel, id est Christi adventum, et liberationem ac spiritualem consolationem quam ex Christi adventu consequerentur Judæi, videlicet redemptionem a peccatis, a diabolo, ab inferno, atque æternæ adeptionem salutis. Aliqui autem Judæi carnales putabant Christum venturum, ut erueret eos de omni subjectione qua alienis gentibus ac principibus subdebantur, universaque mundi regna ipsis subjiceret, quasi in hoc felicitas humana consisteret, vel ob talem liberationem agendam Christus esset promissus, et non potius ad liberandum genus humanum ab originali reatu peccati, et de omni ferocitate diaboli. Talem ergo consolationem Simeon iste non exspectavit, ut etiam Gregorius Nyssenus testatur. Et Spiritus Sanctus erat in eo, non solum per essentiam, præsentiam, et potentiam, quomodo in omni est creatura, nec solum per caritatem et gratiam qualemcumque, prout est in omni eo qui est in statu salutis, seu in caritate, quæ vita est animæ, sed per gratiam eminentem, et caritatem ardentem, secundum quod est in viris heroicis seu perfectis. Habuit quoque gratiam prophetiæ, ut statim dicetur.
paras.en: [[2:25|waiting for the consolation of Israel|exspectans consolationem Israël]]: that is, most surely and lovingly hoping for and awaiting the consolation of Israel, namely the coming of Christ, and the deliverance and spiritual consolation which the Jews would gain from Christ's coming: redemption from sins, from the devil, from hell, and the attaining of eternal salvation. Some carnal Jews, however, thought that Christ would come to rescue them from every subjection by which they were subject to foreign nations and princes, and to subject all the kingdoms of the world to them; as if human happiness consisted in this, or as if Christ had been promised to work such a deliverance, and not rather to deliver mankind from the guilt of original sin and from all the fierceness of the devil. Such a consolation, then, this Simeon did not await, as Gregory of Nyssa also testifies. [[2:25|And the Holy Ghost was in him|Et Spiritus Sanctus erat in eo]]: not only by essence, presence and power, as He is in every creature; nor only by charity and grace of whatever degree, as He is in everyone who is in the state of salvation, or in charity, which is the life of the soul; but by eminent grace and burning charity, as He is in heroic or perfect men. He had also the grace of prophecy, as will be said at once.

paras.t: Et responsum acceperat a Spiritu Sancto non visurum, hoc est non passurum seu experturum, se mortem: visus namque pro quolibet sensu accipitur; nisi prius videret oculis corporalibus atque mentalibus Christum Dominum, qui est omnium Dominus, etiam secundum naturam humanam omni creaturæ prælatus; vel, Christum Domini, hoc est unctum secundum humanitatem a Domino Deo Patre seu tota superbeatissima Trinitate. Porro idem significant, Messias Hebraice, Christus Græce, et unctus Latine. Simeon itaque, sicut et ceteri Patriarchæ, Prophetæ ac Sancti veteris Testamenti, maximo flagrabat desiderio Christi venturi seu ejus adventus. Propter quod Christus ait Apostolis: Beati oculi qui vident quæ vos videtis: dico enim vobis, quia multi reges et Prophetæ voluerunt videre quæ vos videtis, et non viderunt. Idcirco frequenter atque ardenter orabant pro Christi adventu, præsertim Simeon iste, qui ex Scripturis veteris Testamenti agnovit instare Christi adventum. Unde pro merito suæ devotionis facta est sibi revelatio cœlestis a Spiritu Sancto: vel immediate a Spiritu Sancto per illuminationem internam, vel angelo mediante, secundum quod propheticæ revelationes communiter angelorum ministerio factæ sunt, ut S. Dionysius docet. Denique, quamvis opera sanctæ Trinitatis sint indivisa, tamen revelationes hujusmodi appropriantur Spiritui Sancto, quoniam ei appropriantur bonitas, caritas, liberalitas, a quibus donationes directe procedunt.
paras.en: [[2:26|And he had received an answer from the Holy Ghost|Et responsum acceperat a Spiritu Sancto]], [[2:26|that he should not see death|non visurum se mortem]], that is, not suffer or experience it, for *seeing* is taken for any of the senses; [[2:26|before he had seen|nisi prius videret]], with the eyes of the body and of the mind, *Christ the Lord*, who is Lord of all[[Acts 10:36||]], set above every creature even according to His human nature; or [[2:26|the Christ of the Lord|Christum Domini]], that is, anointed according to His humanity by the Lord God the Father, or by the whole most blessed Trinity. Now *Messias* in Hebrew, *Christus* in Greek and *unctus* in Latin mean the same thing [“anointed”]. So Simeon, like the other Patriarchs, Prophets and Saints of the Old Testament, burned with the greatest desire for the Christ who was to come, or for His coming. Wherefore Christ says to the Apostles: [[Luke 10:23|Blessed are the eyes that see the things which you see|Beati oculi qui vident quæ vos videtis]]: [[Luke 10:24|For I say to you that many prophets and kings have desired to see the things that you see and have not seen them|dico enim vobis, quia multi reges et Prophetæ voluerunt videre quæ vos videtis, et non viderunt]]. Therefore they prayed often and ardently for Christ's coming, especially this Simeon, who knew from the Scriptures of the Old Testament that Christ's coming was at hand. Hence, for the merit of his devotion, a heavenly revelation was made to him by the Holy Ghost: either immediately by the Holy Ghost, through inward enlightenment, or through an angel, in the way that prophetic revelations were commonly made by the ministry of angels, as St Dionysius teaches. Lastly, although the works of the holy Trinity are undivided, yet revelations of this kind are appropriated to the Holy Ghost, because to Him are appropriated goodness, charity and liberality, from which gifts directly proceed.

paras.t: Et venit in Spiritu, hoc est Spiritus Sancti instinctu: quo revelante intellexit adesse horam impletionis promissionis sibi factæ de Christi adspectu; in templum. Et quum inducerent puerum Jesum parentes ejus in templum, scilicet Maria et Joseph, quorum unus tunc tulit Jesum, et puto quod Mater. Cur autem Joseph parens seu pater Christi vocetur, expressum est. Ut facerent secundum consuetudinem legis pro eo, offerendo, ut dictum est, par turturum aut duos pullos columbarum, redimendoque puerum quinque siclis, ut dictum est. Et ipse Simeon, affectuosissime, devotissime, reverendissime, ac jucundissime, accepit eum in ulnas suas, hoc est inter brachia sua, quamvis se contactu Sancti Sanctorum putaret indignum; sed vehemens amor rationem devicit, et ad unionem amplexumque impulit; et benedixit Deum, hoc est, laudavit, gratias egit, et sequens canticum cecinit pro impletione divini promissi et ceteris beneficiis Dei, itemque quia jam plus accepit quam sibi fuit promissum. Promissum siquidem sibi fuit, quod Christum videret; et jam non solum vidit, sed brachiis strinxit, portavit, contrectavit, et puto quod et osculatus sit infantem dulcissimum.
paras.en: [[2:27|And he came by the Spirit|Et venit in Spiritu]], that is, at the prompting of the Holy Ghost, by whose revelation he understood that the hour had come for the fulfilment of the promise made to him of seeing Christ, [[2:27|into the temple|in templum]]. [[2:27|And when his parents brought in the child Jesus|Et quum inducerent puerum Jesum parentes ejus]] into the temple, namely Mary and Joseph, one of whom then carried Jesus, and I think it was the Mother. Why Joseph is called the parent or father of Christ has been explained. [[2:27|to do for him according to the custom of the law|Ut facerent secundum consuetudinem legis pro eo]], by offering, as has been said, a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons, and by redeeming the child with five sicles, as has been said. [[2:28|He also took him into his arms|et ipse accepit eum in ulnas suas]]: Simeon himself, most lovingly, devoutly, reverently and joyfully, took Him into his arms, that is, between his arms, though he thought himself unworthy to touch the Holy of Holies; but vehement love overcame reason and drove him to union and embrace; [[2:28|and blessed God|et benedixit Deum]], that is, praised Him, gave thanks, and sang the following canticle for the fulfilment of the divine promise and God's other benefits, and also because he had now received more than had been promised him. For it had been promised him that he would see Christ; and now he not only saw Him, but clasped Him in his arms, carried Him, touched Him, and I think he even kissed the sweetest child.

paras.t: Et ait: Nunc, postquam tuum promissum implesti, Christum mihi monstrando ut promisisti, dimittis, id est, statim dimittes, vel, supplico ut dimittas me, servum tuum, non servitute servilis timoris, qui metuit pœnam magis quam Dei offensam seu culpam (de quo ait Salvator apud Joannem: Servus non manet in domo in æternum, filius autem manet in domo in æternum; et alibi, Jam non dicam vos servos, sed amicos), sed servum servitute filialis timoris: cui servo ait Salvator, Euge, serve bone et fidelis, intra in gaudium Domini tui; Domine, Deus Pater seu Trinitas Deus, secundum verbum tuum, in pace, hoc est a mundi hujus inquietudine, tribulatione et vitiis eripi, quiescere, seu mortis somno cessare, et in limbo patrum sinuque Abrahæ repausare in dulci spe, quum certus sim cito per Christum inde educi, ad gloriamque transferri. Sic ergo, Dimittis me in pace, secundum verbum tuum, hoc est secundum quod mihi dixisti, quod mortem non experirer, nisi prius Christum viderem: per quod insinuasti, quod Christo viso, mox obdormirem in Domino.
paras.en: *And said*: [[2:29|Now|Nunc]], since Thou hast fulfilled Thy promise, showing me Christ as Thou didst promise, [[2:29|thou dost dismiss|dimittis]], that is, Thou wilt at once dismiss, or, I beseech Thee to dismiss, me, [[2:29|thy servant|servum tuum]]: not by the servitude of servile fear, which dreads punishment more than offending God or guilt (of which the Saviour says in John: [[John 8:35|the servant abideth not in the house for ever: but the son abideth for ever|Servus non manet in domo in æternum, filius autem manet in domo in æternum]]; and elsewhere: [[John 15:15|I will not now call you servants|Jam non dicam vos servos]], but friends), but a servant by the servitude of filial fear: to which servant the Saviour says: [[Matt 25:23|Well done, good and faithful servant|Euge, serve bone et fidelis]], [[Matt 25:23|Enter thou into the joy of thy lord|intra in gaudium Domini tui]]. [[2:29|O Lord|Domine]], God the Father, or God the Trinity, [[2:29|according to thy word in peace|secundum verbum tuum, in pace]]: that is, to be snatched from the unrest, tribulation and vices of this world, to rest, or to cease in the sleep of death, and to repose in the limbo of the fathers and the bosom of Abraham in sweet hope, since I am sure of being soon led out thence by Christ and carried over to glory. So, then: Thou dost dismiss me in peace, according to Thy word, that is, according to what Thou didst tell me, that I should not experience death before I had seen Christ[[2:26||]]; by which Thou didst give me to understand that, once Christ was seen, I should soon fall asleep in the Lord.

paras.t: Quia viderunt oculi mei exteriores et interiores salutare tuum, id est Christum salvatorem: qui dicitur Salutare tuum, quia per ipsum decrevisti mundum salvare, omniumque salutem constituisti in eo. De quo fertur in Psalmo: Notum fecit Dominus salutare suum. Unde et in Genesi Jacob patriarcha testatur: Salutare tuum exspectabo, Domine. Cui Salutari loquitur Pater per Isaiam: Dedi te in lucem gentium, ut sis salus mea usque ad extremum terræ. Hoc Salutare Simeon corporaliter ac intellectualiter vidit. Christus namque in una persona est Deus et homo: ideo, dum homo videbatur oculo corporali, eodem oculo videbatur et Deus, quamvis non secundum divinitatem ipsius; imo secundum Ambrosium, dum caro videtur, videtur et Verbum. Hinc quod apud Joannem habetur, Deum nemo vidit unquam, de Deo secundum divinitatis essentiam dicitur. Insuper, oculo interiori vidit Simeon Salvatorem, quia per fidem cognovit ipsius divinitatem, ejus quoque humanitatem intellectualiter consideravit, et quod a Verbo esset assumpta, pensavit. Hinc de Christo scriptum est in Baruch: Post hæc in terris visus est, et cum hominibus conversatus est; itemque in Isaia, Simul laudabunt, quia oculo ad oculum videbunt.
paras.en: [[2:30|Because my eyes have seen|Quia viderunt oculi mei]], my outward and inward eyes, [[2:30|thy salvation|salutare tuum]], that is, Christ the Saviour, who is called *Thy salvation* because through Him Thou hast decreed to save the world, and hast set the salvation of all in Him. Of whom it is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 97:2|The Lord hath made known his salvation|Notum fecit Dominus salutare suum]]. Hence in Genesis too Jacob the patriarch testifies: [[Gen 49:18|I will look for thy salvation, O Lord.|Salutare tuum expectabo, Domine.]] [the margin reads Gen. xx, 13; the words are Gen 49:18]. To this Salvation the Father speaks through Isaias: [[Is 49:6|I have given thee to be the light of the Gentiles, that thou mayst be my salvation even to the farthest part of the earth|Dedi te in lucem gentium, ut sis salus mea usque ad extremum terræ]]. This Salvation Simeon saw bodily and with the understanding. For Christ is God and man in one person: so when the man was seen with the bodily eye, God too was seen with the same eye, though not according to His divinity; nay, according to Ambrose, when the flesh is seen, the Word is seen too. Hence what we have in John, [[John 1:18|No man hath seen God at any time|Deum nemo vidit unquam]], is said of God according to the essence of the divinity [the margin gives also I Joann. iv, 12, where the same words occur]. Moreover, Simeon saw the Saviour with the inward eye, because by faith he knew His divinity, and also considered His humanity with his understanding, and pondered that it had been assumed by the Word. Hence it is written of Christ in Baruch: [[Bar 3:38|Afterwards he was seen upon earth, and conversed with men|Post hæc in terris visus est, et cum hominibus conversatus est]]; and likewise in Isaias: [[Is 52:8|they shall praise together: for they shall see eye to eye|Simul laudabunt, quia oculo ad oculum videbunt]].

paras.t: Quod parasti, hoc est, per incarnationem videri et agnosci aptum fecisti, seu manifestare disposuisti ac decrevisti, ante faciem omnium populorum, id est in conspectu hominum universorum, seu clare cunctis hominibus, non solum Judæis, sed etiam gentilibus: sic tamen, ut sit distributio accommoda, seu pro generibus singulorum, non pro singulis generum, juxta quem modum in Daniele legitur: Omnes populi, tribus et linguæ servient ei. Deus ergo Pater Unigenitum suum, in divinitate incomprehensibilem atque inaccessibilem lucem inhabitantem, per hoc fecit hominibus manifestum, visibilem et cohabitantem, quod eum humanæ conjunxit naturæ in unitate personæ. Quod ab Isaia ita prædictum est: Paravit Dominus brachium sanctum suum in oculis omnium gentium. Brachium enim Domini, est unicus Filius Dei Patris, per quem Pater omnia fecit, sicut et digitus Dei est Spiritus Sanctus, per quem cuncta revelat. De quo brachio ait Psalmista: Salvavit sibi dextera ejus et brachium sanctum ejus. Pater ergo paravit Salutare hoc ante faciem omnium populorum, quibus per Apostolos prædicatus est Christus, juxta illud Psalmi: In omnem terram exivit sonus eorum; et rursus, Viderunt omnes termini terræ salutare Dei nostri. Quod et in Isaia habetur: Videbunt omnes fines terræ salutare Dei nostri.
paras.en: [[2:31|Which thou hast prepared|Quod parasti]], that is, which by the incarnation Thou hast made fit to be seen and known, or hast disposed and decreed to make manifest, [[2:31|before the face of all peoples|ante faciem omnium populorum]], that is, in the sight of all men, or clearly to all men, not only to the Jews but also to the Gentiles: yet so that the distribution is a fitting one, “for the kinds of individual things, not for the individuals of each kind” [that is, *all peoples* means some of every people, not every single man], in the way in which we read in Daniel: [[Dan 7:14|all peoples, tribes, and tongues shall serve him|Omnes populi, tribus et linguæ servient ei]]. So God the Father made His Only-begotten, incomprehensible in His divinity and dwelling in light inaccessible[[1 Tim 6:16||]], manifest to men, visible and dwelling among them, by joining Him to human nature in unity of person. Which was foretold thus by Isaias: [[Is 52:10|The Lord hath prepared his holy arm in the sight of all the Gentiles|Paravit Dominus brachium sanctum suum in oculis omnium gentium]]. For the arm of the Lord is the only Son of God the Father, through whom the Father made all things, as the finger of God is the Holy Ghost, through whom He reveals all things. Of which arm the Psalmist says: [[Ps 97:1|His right hand hath wrought for him salvation, and his arm is holy|Salvavit sibi dextera ejus et brachium sanctum ejus]]. The Father, then, prepared this Salvation before the face of all peoples, to whom Christ was preached by the Apostles, according to that of the Psalm: [[Ps 18:5|Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth|In omnem terram exivit sonus eorum]]; and again: [[Ps 97:3|All the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God|Viderunt omnes termini terræ salutare Dei nostri]]. Which we have also in Isaias: [[Is 52:10|all the ends of the earth shall see the salvation of our God|Videbunt omnes fines terræ salutare Dei nostri]].

paras.t: Quamvis interea Christus ita paratus sit ante omnium faciem populorum, aliter tamen quantum ad Judæos, et aliter quoad gentes. Propter quod subditur: Lumen ad revelationem gentium, hoc est, Salutare seu Christum parasti sic, ut specialiter sit lumen gentilium, seu ad illuminationem eorum qui veri Dei cognitione et cultu privati, idola coluerunt ac dæmones. Sed Christus per suos discipulos reduxit illos ad veri Dei cognitionem, amorem et cultum; imo per interiorem suam illuminationem hoc potius fecit, sine qua exterior Apostolorum prædicatio nihil juvisset; sed et Trinitas Deus merito conversationis passionisque Christi, tantam dedit gentilibus gratiam. Ideo Christus paratus et datus est lumen ad revelationem seu illuminationem gentilium, qui sedebant in tenebris perfidiæ, erroris ac omnium vitiorum. Unde in Isaia Dominus protestatur: Ecce testem populis dedi eum, ducem ac præceptorem gentibus. — Insuper parasti Salutare hoc, gloriam plebis tuæ Israel, id est ad hoc, ut sit gloria Israeliticæ plebis: quæ fuit specialiter plebs Dei, ut plenius dictum est super illud, Visitavit et fecit redemptionem plebis suæ. Hoc enim est plebi illi, quantum ad eos qui crediderunt ex ea, præcipua prærogativa, exaltatio, honor et gloria, quod Unigenitus Dei ex ea incarnari elegit, ad eam personaliter venit, propter eam primo ac specialiter descendit, secundum quod loquitur Dominus: Non sum missus nisi ad oves quæ perierunt domus Israel. Insuper fuit in gloriam plebis suæ Israel, quia per ipsum sancti veteris Testamenti in limbo detenti, adepti sunt beatificæ gloriam visionis. — Denique Christus tam Judæis quam gentibus fuit lumen et gloria. Omnes enim electi, per ipsum sunt illustrati; et cunctis gloria est, quod Dei Filius humanam naturam assumpsit. Nihilo minus per appropriationem dicitur lumen gentium, et gloria Judæorum. Propter quod ait Joannes: Salus ex Judæis est.
paras.en: Although Christ, meanwhile, was thus prepared before the face of all peoples, yet it was in one way as regards the Jews and in another as regards the Gentiles. Wherefore there follows: [[2:32|A light to the revelation of the Gentiles|Lumen ad revelationem gentium]]: that is, Thou hast so prepared the Salvation, or Christ, that He may be especially the light of the Gentiles, or for the enlightenment of those who, deprived of the knowledge and worship of the true God, worshipped idols and demons. But Christ, through His disciples, brought them back to the knowledge, love and worship of the true God; nay rather, He did this by His inward enlightenment, without which the outward preaching of the Apostles would have availed nothing; and God the Trinity, by the merit of Christ's life and passion, gave such grace to the Gentiles. Therefore Christ was prepared and given as a light to the revelation or enlightenment of the Gentiles, who sat in the darkness of unbelief, of error and of all vices. Hence in Isaias the Lord declares: [[Is 55:4|Behold I have given him for a witness to the people, for a leader and a master to the Gentiles.|Ecce testem populis dedi eum, ducem ac præceptorem gentibus.]] — Moreover, Thou hast prepared this Salvation as [[2:32|the glory of thy people Israel|gloriam plebis tuæ Israel]], that is, to this end, that He may be the glory of the people of Israel: which was especially the people of God, as was said more fully on the words *He hath visited and wrought the redemption of his people*[[Luke 1:68||]]. For this is the chief prerogative, exaltation, honour and glory of that people, as regards those of it who believed: that the Only-begotten of God chose to become incarnate from it, came to it in person, and came down first and especially for its sake, according to what the Lord says: [[Matt 15:24|I was not sent but to the sheep, that are lost of the house of Israel|Non sum missus nisi ad oves quæ perierunt domus Israel]]. Further, He was for the glory of His people Israel because through Him the saints of the Old Testament held in limbo attained the glory of the beatific vision. — Lastly, Christ was light and glory to Jews and Gentiles alike. For all the elect are enlightened by Him; and it is a glory to all that the Son of God took human nature. Nevertheless, by appropriation He is called the light of the Gentiles and the glory of the Jews. Wherefore John says: [[John 4:22|salvation is of the Jews|Salus ex Judæis est]] [Denis says “John”, meaning the Gospel of John, where Christ speaks these words].

paras.t: Potest autem hic quæri, quomodo Simeon, templum ingressus, cognovit puerum Jesum quem ante non vidit. Ad quod facile respondetur, quod eodem Spiritu revelante, quo cognovit esse venturum. Et forte aliquod signum sensibile fuit sibi divinitus prænuntiatum, quo cognosceret puerum: sicut Joanni Baptistæ Deus prædixit, Super quem videris Spiritum descendentem et manentem, hic est, etc. Forsitan namque vidit divinum quemdam splendorem in vultu pueri adorandi. De quo aliquando verum fuit dicere: Hic est infans unius diei et Deus æternus.
paras.en: Here it may be asked how Simeon, on entering the temple, knew the child Jesus, whom he had not seen before. To this the answer is easy: by the revelation of the same Spirit by whom he knew that He was to come. And perhaps some sensible sign had been foretold him by God, by which he might know the child: as God foretold to John the Baptist: [[John 1:33|He upon whom thou shalt see the Spirit descending and remaining upon him, he it is|Super quem videris Spiritum descendentem et manentem, hic est]], etc. For perhaps he saw a certain divine splendour in the face of the child he was to adore; of whom it was once true to say: This is an infant of one day, and the eternal God.

paras.t: Postremo, quilibet nostrum canticum istud dicere in propria potest persona, loquendo ad Deum Patrem seu Trinitatem: Nunc, id est in tempore gratiæ hujus, dimittis servum tuum, Domine, secundum verbum tuum, in pace: hoc est, in pectoris tranquillitate quam mihi donasti, me modo, ut spero et oro, quiescere gratiose permittes ac facies, ne turber aut ruam, sed in pace in id ipsum dormiam et requiescam, atque in omni adversitate, tentatione et inquietudine, mens mea, quieta et fixa persistat in te; secundum verbum tuum, hoc est, prout in te plene sperantibus promisisti, quibus tuam defensionem ubertim in Scripturis promittis, juxta illud in Psalmo: Quoniam in me speravit, liberabo eum; protegam eum, quoniam cognovit nomen meum, etc. Quia viderunt oculi mei interiores per fidem, per sapientiæ donum, per Scripturarum doctrinam, per sacramentales species, variosque supernaturales tuos effectus, salutare tuum, quia his modis jam Christum cognoscimus. Cetera verba cantici hujus aliam interpretationem non flagitant.
paras.en: Lastly, any one of us can say this canticle in his own person, speaking to God the Father, or to the Trinity: [[2:29|Now thou dost dismiss thy servant, O Lord|Nunc dimittis servum tuum Domine]], that is, *now*, in this time of grace, [[2:29|according to thy word in peace|secundum verbum tuum, in pace]]: that is, in the tranquillity of heart which Thou hast given me, Thou wilt now graciously let me rest, and make me rest, as I hope and pray, so that I be not troubled nor fall, but [[Ps 4:9|In peace in the self same I will sleep, and I will rest|in pace in id ipsum dormiam et requiescam]], and in all adversity, temptation and disquiet my mind may remain quiet and fixed in Thee; *according to thy word*, that is, as Thou hast promised to those who hope fully in Thee, to whom in the Scriptures Thou promisest Thy protection abundantly, according to that in the Psalm: [[Ps 90:14|Because he hoped in me I will deliver him: I will protect him because he hath known my name|Quoniam in me speravit, liberabo eum; protegam eum, quoniam cognovit nomen meum]], etc. [[2:30|Because my eyes have seen|Quia viderunt oculi mei]], my inward eyes, by faith, by the gift of wisdom, by the teaching of the Scriptures, by the sacramental species, and by Thy various supernatural works, [[2:30|thy salvation|salutare tuum]]: for in these ways we now know Christ. The other words of this canticle call for no other interpretation.

paras.t: Convenientissime demum statutum est canticum istud in Completorio diei, quia tunc cum præcipua pace interna Deo vacare, ad stratumque ire, ac obdormire, et Christum in pectore nostro quasi sepelire debemus, omni tentatione, aversione et culpa prorsus exclusis. Tunc ergo canticum istud compendiosum atque dulcissimum devotissime proferamus, et qualiter Simeon beatissimus Christum in brachiis strinxit, ac cetera quæ dicta sunt, contigerunt, intentissime recordemur, et quæ Simeon corporaliter fecit, spiritualiter peragamus. Itaque et nos puerum Jesum brachiis fidei caritatisque apprehendamus, deosculemur, stringamus ad pectus, imo in pectoris secretissimo collocemus, dicentes cum Sponsa, juxta illud: Fasciculus myrrhæ dilectus meus mihi, inter ubera mea commorabitur. Verum qui hoc agere cupit ac debet, oportet ut commune bonum Ecclesiæ cordialiter optet, quærat et oret, atque a Spiritu Sancto agatur, et carnali consolatione contempta, spiritualem dumtaxat exspectet. Non enim in Deo delectari valet sinceriter, cui oblectamenta carnis aut sæculi placent, vel qui in vanis cogitationibus gloriatur. — Adhuc autem canticum istud post celebrationem seu communionem et hora mortis jam proxima aptissime dicitur, quemadmodum consideranti sensum ejus patescit.
paras.en: Most fittingly, then, has this canticle been appointed for Compline, at the close of the day: for then, with a special inward peace, we ought to give ourselves to God, go to our bed and fall asleep, and as it were bury Christ in our breast, with every temptation, turning away and fault wholly shut out. Then, therefore, let us most devoutly utter this short and most sweet canticle, and recall most attentively how most blessed Simeon held Christ tight in his arms, and how the other things that have been told came about; and what Simeon did bodily, let us do spiritually. So let us too take the child Jesus in the arms of faith and charity, kiss Him, press Him to our breast, nay, place Him in the most secret part of our heart, saying with the Bride: [[Cant 1:12|A bundle of myrrh is my beloved to me, he shall abide between my breasts|Fasciculus myrrhæ dilectus meus mihi, inter ubera mea commorabitur]]. But whoever desires to do this, and ought to, must heartily wish for, seek and pray for the common good of the Church, and be led by the Holy Ghost, and, despising carnal consolation, look for the spiritual alone. For he cannot take a sincere delight in God who is pleased by the delights of the flesh or of the world, or who glories in vain thoughts. — Further, this canticle is most fittingly said after celebrating Mass or receiving communion, and when the hour of death is near, as is plain to one who considers its sense.

paras.t: Præterea, aliqui in primo hujus cantici versiculo, per Dominum intelligunt Christum, ita quod Simeon puerum Jesum quem inter brachia complectebatur, Deum ac Dominum nominavit. Tuncque per salutare Domini intelligitur Incarnationis mysterium, vel assumpta humanitas: per quod, seu quam, velut per instrumentum ac medium, Verbum æternum operatum est mundi salutem, gentium illuminationem, Judæorumque glorificationem. Vel salutare hoc esset salus seu redemptio tunc fienda per Christum, quam Simeon spiritu prophetali prævidit.
paras.en: Besides, some understand *Lord* in the first verse of this canticle as Christ, so that Simeon called the child Jesus, whom he held in his arms, God and Lord. And then by the *salvation* of the Lord is understood the mystery of the Incarnation, or the humanity assumed: by which, as by an instrument and means, the eternal Word wrought the salvation of the world, the enlightenment of the Gentiles and the glorifying of the Jews.
